description: ¡Hola! Somos SoftwArt, un equipo apasionado por el desarrollo de software, el diseño y la tecnología. Nos estamos uniendo al NASA Space Apps Challenge para construir soluciones innovadoras y creativas orientadas al impacto espacial. Buscamos compañeras entusiastas y con buena onda que quieran aportar su talento en programación, diseño o análisis para armar un proyecto increíble juntas. ¡Escríbenos para sumarte!
summary: ASTRA HEALTH is a health monitoring dashboard designed for astronauts on space missions, created for the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" challenge. It lets users log seven indicators (pulse, blood pressure, temperature, oxygen saturation, glucose, muscle mass, and sleep) by typing or speaking: the assistant "Astra" responds to a wake word, converses in Spanish and English, and asks for confirmation before saving any data. Its analysis engine is deterministic: trends, averages, and changes between records, separating non-comparable contexts (rest vs. exercise, fasting vs. after meals) and flagging anything it cannot process as "requires review." Educational explanations cite public sources (NASA Human Research Program, NASA-STD-3001, MedlinePlus, WHO), and a read-only connector to the NASA Open Science Data Repository allows users to consult real studies (OSD-656, OSD-48) with dates and provenance. It includes an interactive 3D human body, trend charts, alerts, mission challenges with badges, and a wellness guide. It uses synthetic demonstration data; it is not a medical device.
details:
What did we develop and how does it work?

We developed a web prototype that brings health indicator tracking and wellness monitoring together in a mission interface. The crew member enters readings by typing or voice: the "Astra" assistant asks which instrument the reading came from and requests confirmation before saving any data. The analysis engine is local and deterministic: it calculates averages, minimums, maximums, and changes between readings, distinguishes non-comparable contexts (rest vs. exercise, fasting vs. after eating), and marks anything it cannot process as "requires review." It includes a 3D human body explorer, a monitor with trend charts, alerts, a mood journal, challenges with badges, a wellness guide, PDF export, and a read-only connector to the NASA Open Science Data Repository for consulting real space studies with their provenance. The interface is bilingual (Spanish and English).

What benefits does it offer and what impact does it seek?

It supports the crew in recording and reviewing their own indicators during long missions, with hands-free voice logging and simple explanations that cite their source and date. We aim to explore how to present health information in an understandable way without attributing diagnostic capabilities to the prototype: it does not measure, diagnose, or replace the medical team, and the demonstration data are synthetic and labeled.

What tools and programming languages do we use?

Backend in Python with FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, SQLite, and Pydantic; frontend in React and Vite, with Three.js and React Three Fiber for the 3D body, jsPDF, and Lucide; voice with the browser's Web Speech API and MediaRecorder; tests with pytest, Ruff, node:test, and Playwright. Optional integration with Groq, OpenAI, and Gemini APIs; without them, it works with the local extractor. Sources: NASA OSDR, NASA Human Research Program, NASA-STD-3001, NTRS reports, JAXA, WHO, MedlinePlus, and NHLBI.
